title: ClickHouse vs PostgreSQL: When Does a Database Actually Break Down?
summary: PostgreSQL is fantastic for user logins, orders, and payments. But the moment you ask it to calculate total sales across 50 million rows, queries slow down to a crawl. Here is why the physical way data is stored on disk makes all the difference.
analogyTitle: The Real-Life Analogy: The Spreadsheet vs. The Box of Paper Receipts
analogy:
PostgreSQL (Row Database) puts each customer receipt into its own envelope with name, address, phone, item, and price. If you want to find the average price across 10,000 customers, you have to open all 10,000 envelopes and unfold every single sheet of paper.

ClickHouse (Column Database) keeps one single sheet of paper that lists ONLY prices in a clean column. Calculating the average takes 1 second because you only read the price sheet without touching names or addresses.

sections.heading: 1. Row-Oriented (Postgres) vs Column-Oriented (ClickHouse)
sections.content: Hard drives and SSDs read data in chunks (blocks). In a row database, every attribute of user #1 sits right next to user #1's address. To sum 1 column, the database is forced to read all 40 columns from disk.

sections.heading: 2. The Golden Rule of System Design
sections.content:
• Use PostgreSQL when you need ACID consistency, updating individual customer records, and user checkout carts (OLTP).
• Use ClickHouse when you are streaming millions of events, analytics logs, or generating aggregated dashboards in milliseconds (OLAP).

takeaway: Never force an OLTP transactional database to do heavy analytical aggregations. Keep transactional data in Postgres and stream historical events to ClickHouse.
